title: Trendline Break
teaches: The trendline break as we trade it: a leader above its 200-day drifts tight under a falling line drawn over the daily highs, the buy is the trade through the line and the prior day's high at market in regular hours and never more than 4% past the line, the stop sits a few cents under the trigger day's low, a close back under the line is a warning and not an exit, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a break on its own is a warning, not a reversal.

sources.title: John Murphy's Law #5 - Draw the Line (Trendlines) (2025-11-21)
Gold Trendline - Bogus or Bullish? (2017-06-12)
sources.why_reliable: A veteran classical chartist writing in his own name; futures-first, experience rather than a study, so it supports a view and never carries a key alone.

facts.quote: A downtrend line has a negative slope formed by connecting two or more high points.
facts.claim: ChartSchool: a downtrend line slopes down and connects high points.

facts.quote: As the steepness of a trend line increases, the validity of the support or resistance level decreases.
facts.claim: ChartSchool: the steeper the line, the less valid it is.

facts.quote: Trend line breaks should not be the final arbiter, but should serve merely as a warning that a change in trend may be imminent.
facts.claim: ChartSchool: a break is a warning, not the final arbiter.

facts.quote: Sometimes, the lows or highs don't match up, and it is best not to force the issue.
facts.claim: ChartSchool: when the highs do not match up, do not force the line.

facts.quote: If the points of contact between price and trendlines are too close, the move might be nothing more than noise.
facts.claim: The Insider: touches too close together may be nothing more than noise.

facts.quote: When a trendline breaks, treat it as a heads-up, not a trading signal.
facts.claim: The Insider: a break is a heads-up, not a trading signal.

facts.quote: A trendline break with volume matters more than a break without.
facts.claim: The Insider: a break with volume matters more than a break without.

facts.quote: proper trendlines are drawn between intervening lows of roughly equal magnitudes and should never be forced.
facts.claim: CMT: proper trendlines should never be forced.

facts.quote: down-sloping trendlines are drawn above the peaks, not below the valleys.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: a down-sloping trendline is drawn above the peaks.

facts.quote: If you use the start (top) of the trendline, price reaches it 77% of the time.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: price reaches the start of the line 77% of the time.

facts.quote: The violation of a trendline does not carry with it a price target
facts.claim: Brandt: a trendline break carries no price target.

facts.quote: It is best to avoid a downtrend when the moving averages act as resistance, guiding the stock lower.
facts.claim: Kell: avoid a downtrend when the averages act as resistance.

facts.quote: As the index forms a Wedge Pop, the strongest stocks will break out from their bases and make new highs.
facts.claim: Kell: as the index forms a Wedge Pop, the strongest stocks break out.

facts.quote: Stop first (by default a few cents under the day's low or the prior day's low, F62); the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
facts.claim: A3: stop first, a few cents under the day's low; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.

facts.quote: The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule (B20).
facts.claim: A4: the stop is the exit; it only moves up, never wider; the gap rule is the one exception.

facts.quote: Shares = account × risk % ÷ (entry − stop), rounded down, then capped: the size is the SMALLER of the risk-based size and the position cap
facts.claim: A5: shares are account times risk percent, divided by entry minus stop, rounded down, then capped.

facts.quote: "I almost never take a loss greater than 3%": the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy (a loss on the position, not the account).
facts.claim: A13: the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy.

facts.quote: Move the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, ideally. The first trim: the hard rule is a third at 3R; ideally anywhere from 3R to 6R, and in practice he mostly waits for 5R.
facts.claim: B19: breakeven between 2R and 5R; the hard rule for the first trim is a third at 3R.

facts.quote: A gap against the stop: the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day decide. The low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop.
facts.claim: B20: on a gap through the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop.

facts.quote: With a ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.
facts.claim: B20's ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.

facts.quote: No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report; hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R.
facts.claim: B22: no new buys in the 3 days before a report; hold through one only if up 5R.

facts.quote: Trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
facts.claim: B23: only stocks at $10 or more trading at least $20 million a day.

facts.quote: The 200-day line: no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long; shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless it is a parabolic short.
facts.claim: B26: no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, except a parabolic long.

facts.quote: No chasing: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.
facts.claim: C28: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.

facts.quote: Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink (A5).
facts.claim: C28: chasing costs size, because the stop stays put and the distance grows.

facts.quote: Too stretched to buy: skip a long that is more than 10% above its 10-day average.
facts.claim: C29: skip a long more than 10% above its 10-day average.

facts.quote: Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups, except parabolic and mean-reversion trades.
facts.claim: C31: buy leaders, an RS rating of 80 or more in a strong group.

facts.quote: Time stop: a trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
facts.claim: C33: a trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold.

facts.quote: Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head.
facts.claim: D41: a real stop order with the broker.

facts.quote: After the first third at 3R: another third at 5R, then trail the last third; adjustable.
facts.claim: E51: another third at 5R, then trail the last third.

facts.quote: Default trail: the 10-day average for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones; sell on a close below it.
facts.claim: E52: trail the 10-day for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones; sell on a close below it.

facts.quote: Entries are market orders.
facts.claim: E57: entries are market orders.

facts.quote: No new buys outside regular trading hours.
facts.claim: E58: no new buys outside regular hours.

facts.quote: The stop sits a few cents under the day's low, not exactly on it.
facts.claim: F62: the stop sits a few cents under the day's low.

facts.quote: If a stock opens above a trim level (3R, 5R), take that trim at the open.
facts.claim: F63: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.

facts.quote: The market reading as a guide (A10): Green, full risk per grade and up to 10 positions; Yellow, smaller and fewer; Orange, only A+ setups; Red, mostly cash and shorts.
facts.claim: F65: Green full risk; Yellow smaller and fewer; Orange only A+; Red mostly cash and shorts.

facts.quote: After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule.
facts.claim: B21: after a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade.

facts.quote: The same stock: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month.
facts.claim: E56: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month on one stock.

facts.quote: A climax run on your own long (Bracco's parabolic burst): sell a big part into it, a judgment call.
facts.claim: C34: a climax run on your own long: sell a big part into it.

facts.quote: The line is drawn over the daily highs (wicks included) of the pullback or base, starting at its highest high (the left-side high), on a log chart.
facts.claim: Card: the line is drawn over the daily highs, wicks included, starting at the pullback's highest high.

facts.quote: A clean, first break: no daily close above the line between the first anchor and the trigger day. A wick through is allowed.
facts.claim: Card: a first break has no daily close above the line before the trigger day; a wick is allowed.

facts.quote: The anchors are at least 5 sessions apart.
facts.claim: Card: the two anchor highs are at least 5 sessions apart.

facts.quote: Tight under the line: in the 5 sessions before the trigger the closes sit within about 5% under the line and the average daily range is smaller than the 20-session average.
facts.claim: Card: tight under the line means closes close under it and a shrinking daily range.

facts.quote: Not wedging up: rising lows into the line on shrinking volume is not the tight drift down this setup wants.
facts.claim: Card: rising lows into the line on shrinking volume is not the tight drift down we want.

facts.quote: The trigger day closes above the 200-day SMA.
facts.claim: Card: the trigger day closes above the 200-day.

facts.quote: RS rating 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
facts.claim: Card: RS rating 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.

facts.quote: Price $10 or more; at least $20 million traded a day.
facts.claim: Card: price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day.

facts.quote: Not more than 10% above the 10-day average on the trigger day.
facts.claim: Card: not more than 10% above the 10-day average on the trigger day.

facts.quote: No report due in the next 3 sessions.
facts.claim: Card: no earnings report due in the next 3 sessions.

facts.quote: during regular hours price trades above the line's value for the day AND above the prior day's high
facts.claim: Card trigger: during regular hours price trades above the line's value and the prior day's high.

facts.quote: Do not buy more than 4% above the line's value that day, or more than 1.5 ATR above it, whichever is smaller. A gap open more than 4% above the line is no trade.
facts.claim: Card: no buy more than 4% or 1.5 ATR above the line; a gap open over 4% is no trade.

facts.quote: Do not wait for a close 3% past the line. That filter is for long-term lines and would use up most of the 4% chase limit and widen the stop.
facts.claim: Card: do not wait for a close 3% past the line.

facts.quote: A few cents under the trigger day's low as it stands at entry; the prior day's low is the wider choice.
facts.claim: Card: the stop is a few cents under the trigger day's low as it stands at entry.

facts.quote: Size from the stop. If the honest stop is more than about 3%, take the smaller size the formula gives or skip
facts.claim: Card: size from the stop; over about 3%, take the smaller size or skip.

facts.quote: The stop sits with the broker and only moves up.
facts.claim: Card: the stop sits with the broker and only moves up.

facts.quote: A gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if that is past 2R.
facts.claim: Card: a gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R.

facts.quote: Stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R.
facts.claim: Card: stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R.

facts.quote: between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default (B19)
facts.claim: Card: breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.

facts.quote: A third off at 3R.
facts.claim: Card: a third off at 3R.

facts.quote: A third at 5R.
facts.claim: Card: a third at 5R.

facts.quote: A gap over a trim level: trim at the open.
facts.claim: Card: a gap over a trim level: trim at the open.

facts.quote: Trail the last third under the 10-day (fast movers) or 21-day (steadier), selling on a close below it.
facts.claim: Card: trail the last third under the 10-day (fast) or 21-day (steadier), on a close below it.

facts.quote: Time stop: still under 1R after 10 sessions, sell. No follow-through within a few sessions is itself the signal.
facts.claim: Card: still under 1R after 10 sessions, sell; no follow-through is itself the signal.

facts.quote: A climax burst on the way up: sell a big part into it.
facts.claim: Card: a climax burst on the way up: sell a big part into it.

facts.quote: After the entry, a close back under the line is a warning, not an exit. The stop is the exit and only moves up.
facts.claim: Card: a close back under the line is a warning, not an exit; the stop is the exit.

facts.quote: Green market: full. Yellow: smaller and fewer. Orange: A+ only, so a B- is a pass. Red: mostly cash.
facts.claim: Card: Green full; Yellow smaller and fewer; Orange A+ only; Red mostly cash.

facts.quote: A cue: the index itself breaking its own downtrend line or making a wedge pop.
facts.claim: Card: a cue is the index itself breaking its own downtrend line or making a wedge pop.

facts.quote: A break is a first entry, never an add. Full size once, one stop.
facts.claim: Card: a break is a first entry, never an add; full size once, one stop.

facts.quote: After a stop-out, only a new trigger. Do not redraw the same line to get back in. At most 3 tries a week and 6 a month on one stock.
facts.claim: Card: after a stop-out only a new trigger; do not redraw the line to get back in.

facts.quote: Context, not a rule: the first anchor high is overhead supply. Bulkowski found price reached the start of the line 77% of the time; no pattern target replaces the R-based trims.
facts.claim: Card: the first anchor high is overhead supply; no pattern target replaces the R-based trims.

facts.quote: Before the entry: the stock is under falling averages acting as resistance. Not this setup.
facts.claim: Card: a stock under falling averages acting as resistance is not this setup.

facts.quote: A weak-volume break that barely clears the line closes back under it the next day and the stop goes; or three flat closes with no higher high and the time stop.
facts.claim: Card failure mode: a weak-volume break that barely clears the line closes back under it and the stop goes.

facts.quote: Treating any break as a reversal.
facts.claim: Card mistake: treating any break as a reversal.

facts.quote: Buying breaks of steep lines.
facts.claim: Card mistake: buying breaks of steep lines.

facts.quote: A flat base's ceiling is one level touched twice within 0.5 ATR and the buy is the base's highest high; a trendline falls, at least a little, from lower swing highs.
facts.claim: Card: a trendline falls, at least a little, from lower swing highs.

facts.quote: A line with no slope is a horizontal resistance break, not this setup
facts.claim: Card: a line with no slope is a horizontal resistance break, not this setup.

facts.quote: When the line is the top of a flag, the flag is the setup and the line is its trigger.
facts.claim: Card: when the line is the top of a flag, the flag is the setup and the line is its trigger.

facts.quote: A wedge pop comes after a decline with at least 8 of the last 15 closes under the 20 EMA, out of a 3-day or longer tight range, and the pop reclaims the 10 and 20 EMAs
facts.claim: Card: a wedge pop follows a decline with most closes under the 20 EMA and reclaims the 10 and 20 EMAs.

facts.quote: the fast EMAs already reclaimed or held on the trigger day
facts.claim: Card: a trendline break has the fast EMAs already reclaimed or held on the trigger day.

facts.quote: Using the flag's trendline break on a high tight flag. Bulkowski: they fail too often that way; buy the pattern's highest high instead.
facts.claim: Card mistake: using the flag's trendline break on a high tight flag; buy the pattern's highest high instead.

facts.quote: Not ours: the scanner's 2R and 3R targets, Murphy's measuring rule, Bulkowski's 56% measure rule, Weinstein's sell-half-on-the-break.
facts.claim: Card: not ours: the scanner's targets, Murphy's measuring rule, Bulkowski's measure rule.

facts.quote: tl.stop_width: a wide stop (3% to 5% is a B; wider is a B-)
facts.claim: Grading: a stop of 3% to 5% is a B; wider is a B-.

facts.quote: tl.tight_under: price tight under the line for several days on drying volume, the 10 and 21-day EMAs converging under it
facts.claim: Grading A+: price tight under the line on drying volume.

facts.quote: tl.overhead_supply: room to the first anchor high
facts.claim: Grading A+: room to the first anchor high.

facts.quote: tl.overhead_supply: a key level just above (ALAB's below a key level)
facts.claim: Grading B-: a key level just above.

facts.quote: tl.market_reading: Yellow is a B; Orange is a B- (F65 says A+ only there, so a pass)
facts.claim: Grading: Yellow is a B; Orange is a B- and a pass.

facts.claim: MSFT: a mega-cap drifting tightly under a five-month line; 3R came the next day.

facts.claim: MCK: a high-priced leader, a shallow slow line with five touches; the break ran straight to new highs.

facts.quote: above the 10- and 21-day EMAs, above a 200-day SMA that is higher than 20 sessions earlier

facts.quote: The next session opened at 152.00 and fell to 144.06

facts.claim: DHR: the low was 19 cents under the stop, then the stock closed 209.53 and reached 217 within a week.

facts.quote: closed 0.39% over the line (18.85 against 18.78); the next day closed back under it at 18.58 and the stop traded.
facts.claim: LBTYA: the break closed 0.39% over the line; the next day it closed back under it and the stop traded.

facts.quote: the trigger day closes 4.9% under the 200-day SMA; the rule needs a close above it

facts.quote: a good-looking line (4 touches, 102 sessions, 1.32x volume) under a flat 200-day

facts.quote: which is what a fixed stop without trims does and why the house trims a third at 3R and 5R and trails the rest
facts.claim: A fixed stop without trims is why the house trims a third at 3R and 5R and trails the rest.

facts.quote: valid by every gate, stopped by the rules

walkthroughs.title: NUE, October 2006: eight touches, a tight drift
steps: NUE, 2006. A leader pulls back 26% from a 60.30 high. Eight touches over five months build the line.
Price drifts tight under the 106-session line. The break comes off a higher low above the 200-day.
2006-10-05: it trades through 50.47 on 1.8x volume. Buy at market, 50.48. Stop a few cents under the low, 49.20.
Failure mode: a thin break closes back under the line, stop taken. Instead 3R came in 6 sessions. Trim a third.

walkthroughs.title: MSFT, January 2012: the small honest stop
steps: MSFT, 2012. A mega-cap drifts tight under a five-month line, 112 sessions old, with 6 touches.
It is a 16% pullback from 28.15. The drift is quiet, and the daily ranges are small.
2012-01-04: it trades through 26.89 and the prior high. Buy at market, 26.97. Stop a few cents under the low, 26.73.
Failure mode: the break closes back under the line, stop taken. Instead 3R came the next day. Trim a third.

walkthroughs.title: SCHW, February 2020: the planned loss
steps: SCHW, 2020. A leader breaks a 46-session line on 1.81x volume, closing 0.98% over it.
2020-02-20: buy at market, 48.12. Stop a few cents under the day's low, 47.25, 1.80% away.
Failure mode: the next session was day one of the February 2020 market break. The low was 45.93; the stop traded.
A planned loss of 1.80%. The stock fell to 34.45 within 10 sessions. Another buy needs a new trigger.

questions.q: A falling trendline for a breakout is drawn over what?
questions.answer: The daily highs, wicks included
questions.why: The daily highs, wicks included. A downtrend line connects high points, drawn above the peaks and not through price.
questions.lesson_line: Draw it over the highs, wicks and all. Start at the pullback's highest high.

wrong.The daily closes only: A line over the closes cuts through the wicks. The line goes over the highs.
wrong.The daily lows: Lows make a rising line under price. The falling line sits over the highs.
wrong.The 50-day average: An average is not a trendline. The line is drawn on the highs themselves.

questions.q: On its own, a trendline break is a warning, not a reversal.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A break is merely a warning that a change in trend may be imminent. The Insider calls it a heads-up, not a trading signal.
questions.lesson_line: A broken line is a heads-up. It is not a reversal by itself.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on a trendline break bought during the day?
choices: A few cents under the trigger day's low
questions.answer: A few cents under the trigger day's low
questions.why: A few cents under the trigger day's low, as it stands at entry. Not exactly on it, and not on the line.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the trigger day's low.

wrong.Exactly on the line: The line is the trigger, not the stop. A close back under it is a warning; the stop is the exit.
wrong.Under the 200-day average: That is far below the trade. The stop sits close, near the trigger day's low.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: We do not buy a trendline break in a stock under its ___-day average.
questions.why: 200. The trigger day closes above the 200-day. No longs below the 200-day, unless it is a parabolic long.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day first. Then look at the line.

questions.q: We buy trendline breaks in leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in a strong group.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
questions.lesson_line: A clean line in a laggard is still a laggard. Buy the leaders.

questions.q: A trendline break is a good spot to add to a position you already hold.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A break is a first entry, never an add. Full size once, one stop.
questions.lesson_line: Full size once, one stop. A break is an entry, not an add.

questions.q: The stop sits with the broker as a real order, and it only moves up.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head. It only moves up, never down or wider.
questions.lesson_line: A real order with the broker, moved up only.

questions.q: Which event is the buy on a trendline break?
choices: Trades through the line and prior high
Price touches the line from below
questions.answer: Trades through the line and prior high
questions.why: It trades through the line and the prior day's high, during regular hours, bought at market. No close is needed.
questions.lesson_line: Through the line and the prior high, in hours, at market.

wrong.Price touches the line from below: Touching the line is not a break. Price has to trade through it.
wrong.A close 3% past the line: We do not wait for a close 3% past the line. That filter is for long-term lines.
wrong.The 50-day crossing the 200-day: A crossing of averages is a different signal. The trigger is the line and the prior high.

questions.q: We wait for a close 3% past the line before we buy.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Do not wait for a close 3% past the line. That filter is for long-term lines and would use up most of the 4% chase limit.
questions.lesson_line: No 3% filter. Waiting costs most of the chase limit.

questions.q: Two highs fix a falling line. How far apart should they be?
questions.answer: At least 5 sessions
questions.why: At least 5 sessions. Touches too close together may be nothing more than noise.
questions.lesson_line: Space the anchors out. Two highs a few days apart prove nothing.

wrong.Any two days: Points too close together make noise, not a line.
wrong.At least 1 session: One session apart is far too close. The anchors need at least 5.
wrong.At least 3 sessions: Three is still too close. The anchors need at least 5.

questions.q: A wick through the line before the trigger day cancels the first break.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A first break means no daily close above the line before the trigger day. A wick through is allowed.
questions.lesson_line: Closes count, wicks do not. No close above the line before the trigger.

questions.q: We take trendline breaks only in stocks at $10 or more that trade $20 million a day.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Price $10 or more and at least $20 million traded a day.
questions.lesson_line: A clean line in a thin stock is still a thin stock.

questions.q: How far over its 10-day average is too far to buy a break?
questions.answer: More than 10%
questions.why: More than 10% over the 10-day average. Skip a long that stretched.
questions.lesson_line: Stretched is a pass. More than 10% over the 10-day, skip it.

wrong.More than 25%: A long that far over its average is long gone. The line is 10%.

questions.q: It helps when the index itself is breaking its own downtrend line.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The index breaking its own downtrend line or making a wedge pop is a cue. Kell: as the index pops, the strongest stocks break out.
questions.lesson_line: Best when the market breaks its own line too.

questions.q: Which market reading allows a full-size trendline break?
questions.answer: Green
questions.why: Green: full size. Yellow is smaller and fewer, Orange is A+ only, and Red is mostly cash.
questions.lesson_line: Green is full size. Every other color cuts it down.

wrong.Yellow: Yellow is smaller and fewer, not full size.
wrong.Red: Red is mostly cash and shorts.

questions.q: Bought at 26.97 with the stop at 26.73. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 27.69. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. MSFT got there the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: The line's value is 50.00 and the ATR is 1.00. What is the most we pay?
questions.why: 51.50. We never pay more than 4% over the line or more than 1.5 ATR over it, whichever is smaller. Here 1.5 ATR is the smaller.
questions.lesson_line: Two caps, take the smaller. The ATR cap is often the tighter one.

questions.q: After entry, a close back under the line means sell at once.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A close back under the line is a warning, not an exit. The stop is the exit and only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the line is a warning. The stop is the exit.

questions.q: Which lead-in to the line is best?
choices: Tight drift down, volume drying up
Lows rising into the line, volume fading
One big drop into the line
questions.answer: Tight drift down, volume drying up
questions.why: A tight drift down. The closes sit close under the line and the daily ranges shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Tight and quiet under the line. Not rising into it.

wrong.Lows rising into the line, volume fading: That is wedging up into the line, not the tight drift down this setup wants.
wrong.Wide swings under the line: Wide swings are not tight. The average daily range should shrink.
wrong.One big drop into the line: A big drop makes a steep line. The steeper the line, the less valid it is.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A fast mover's last third trails on a close under the ___-day.
questions.why: 10. The 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one. Sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the rising average. Sell the close below it, not the touch.

questions.q: Into a vertical climax burst, we sell a big part of the position.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A climax burst on the way up is for selling into. It is a judgment call, and selling a big part is the rule.
questions.lesson_line: A burst up is for selling into. Take the money.

questions.q: A stock sits under falling 10 and 21-day averages that act as resistance. A line break there is?
questions.answer: Not this setup
questions.why: Not this setup. A stock under falling averages acting as resistance is out. Kell: avoid a downtrend when the averages act as resistance.
questions.lesson_line: Falling averages overhead are supply. Wait for a leader.

wrong.A strong buy: Falling averages above price are supply, not support.
wrong.Fine if volume is big: Volume does not fix a stock under falling averages.

questions.q: If the highs do not line up, we draw the line through the closest points anyway.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. It is best not to force the issue. A proper trendline should never be forced.
questions.lesson_line: No line, no trade. Never force a line through the points.

questions.q: Bought at 109.23 with the stop at 106.79. How far below the buy is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 2.23%. The buy minus the stop, divided by the buy. That is inside the 3% a stop usually sits within.
questions.lesson_line: Buy minus stop, over the buy. Know the distance before you size.

questions.q: Buy the open?
questions.story: The falling line sits at 50.00 today. News gaps the stock open to 52.40.
choices: Buy at market; it has momentum
questions.answer: Pass; 4.8% over the line
questions.why: Pass. A gap open more than 4% above the line is no trade; this one is 4.8% over. Chasing costs size, because the stop stays put.
questions.lesson_line: More than 4% over the line is no trade. Let it go.

wrong.Buy at market; it has momentum: Over the 4% cap, the stop stays far away and the shares shrink. That is a chase.
wrong.Buy half size: Half of a chase is still a chase. The line is 4%.

questions.q: Buy the next break?
questions.story: Your break was stopped on Monday. On Wednesday the stock makes a new high, and you redraw the line through it.
choices: No; a redrawn line is no trigger
Yes; the new line is cleaner
questions.answer: No; a redrawn line is no trigger
questions.why: No. After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger. Do not redraw the same line to get back in.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a reason to redraw the line.

wrong.Yes; the new line is cleaner: Redrawing the line to get back in is the named mistake.
wrong.Yes, with a tighter stop: Tightening the stop does not make a redrawn line a trigger.

questions.q: Is this our trendline break?
questions.story: A stock 20% under its 200-day breaks a 60-session falling line on twice its usual volume.
choices: Yes, if the line is long
questions.answer: No; it is under the 200-day
questions.why: No. The trigger day must close above the 200-day, and we do not buy longs below it. A long line and big volume do not change that.
questions.lesson_line: The 200-day comes first. A beaten-down stock is not our break.

wrong.Yes; the volume is big: Big volume does not lift a stock over its 200-day.
wrong.Yes, if the line is long: A long line does not change the 200-day rule.

questions.q: Trendline break or flat top?
questions.story: Three highs sit at exactly 50.00 over six weeks. You are weighing a buy through 50.00.
choices: A flat-top break, not this setup
questions.answer: A flat-top break, not this setup
questions.why: A flat top. A trendline falls, at least a little, from lower swing highs. A line with no slope is a horizontal resistance break.
questions.lesson_line: No slope, no trendline. Three equal highs are a flat top.

wrong.A trendline break: The highs are level, so there is no falling line to break.
wrong.A wedge pop: A wedge pop follows a decline and reclaims the fast averages. Level highs do not.

questions.q: Bought at 26.97, stop 26.73. The stock trades to 28.17. How many R is that?
questions.why: 5R. Each R is the fill minus the stop. That is where the second third comes off.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 5R is the second trim.

questions.q: The stop moves to breakeven somewhere between 2R and 5R.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim.

questions.q: What does the index break do for your list?
questions.story: The S&P 500 breaks its own downtrend line on a strong day. Your list holds three valid line breaks.
choices: It helps; leaders break out with it
Skip them; it is too late
questions.answer: It helps; leaders break out with it
questions.why: It helps. The index breaking its own downtrend line is a cue, and Kell says the strongest stocks break out as the index pops.
questions.lesson_line: A market that breaks its own line lifts the leaders.

wrong.Nothing; indexes do not matter: The market reading is a guide for every setup, and the index break is a cue for this one.
wrong.Skip them; it is too late: The cue says the strongest stocks break out as the index does. It is a reason to look.

questions.q: Where is the first overhead supply for a falling-line break?
choices: The old high where the line starts
The lowest low under the line
questions.answer: The old high where the line starts
questions.why: The old high where the line starts. Price reached it 77% of the time in Bulkowski's study, so expect a fight there.
questions.lesson_line: The anchor high is overhead. Know where it is before you buy.

wrong.The 200-day average: The 200-day is below a stock that qualifies. Supply sits above.
wrong.Yesterday's low: That is where the stop sits, not supply.
wrong.The lowest low under the line: That low is below the line. Supply sits above, at the old high.

questions.q: Which is the setup, and which is the trigger?
questions.story: A stock jumps 25% in 20 sessions, then drifts for 8 sessions under a falling line of two highs.
choices: Flag is the setup; line is the trigger
Line is the setup; flag is context
questions.answer: Flag is the setup; line is the trigger
questions.why: The flag is the setup and the line is its trigger. A trendline break needs no pole, only a line of lower swing highs.
questions.lesson_line: The flag is the setup. The line is how you get in.

wrong.Line is the setup; flag is context: When the line is the top of a flag, the flag is the setup and the line is its trigger.
wrong.Two setups, two trades: One structure, one trade, one stop. A break is never an add.

questions.q: Trendline break or wedge pop?
questions.story: A stock closed 12 of the last 15 sessions under its 20 EMA. A bar then clears a tight range and both fast averages.
choices: A wedge pop; it reclaimed the averages
questions.answer: A wedge pop; it reclaimed the averages
questions.why: A wedge pop. It follows a decline with at least 8 of the last 15 closes under the 20 EMA and reclaims the 10 and 20 EMAs. A trendline break already holds the fast averages.
questions.lesson_line: Lost the averages, then reclaimed them: that is the pop.

wrong.A trendline break: A trendline break has the fast averages already reclaimed or held on the trigger day. This stock lost them.
wrong.A flat-top break: Nothing here is a level ceiling. The tell is the lost and reclaimed averages.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: The reading is Orange. A valid break has a stop 6% away, and a key level sits just above.
choices: No; a B- is a pass in Orange
questions.answer: No; a B- is a pass in Orange
questions.why: No. In Orange only A+ setups are taken, so a B- is a pass. A stop wider than 5% is a B-, and so is a key level just above.
questions.lesson_line: In an Orange market, only the best setups get through.

wrong.Yes; the line is valid: A valid line is not enough in Orange. It has to grade A+.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not turn a B- into an A+. Orange takes A+ only.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: The honest stop sits 4.5% under the buy. Your usual size would risk too much.
choices: Take the smaller size, or skip
questions.answer: Take the smaller size, or skip
questions.why: Take the smaller size the formula gives, or skip. Never tighten the stop to fit.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size. Never back-fit a tighter stop.

wrong.Tighten the stop to 3%: Tightening the honest stop to fit the size is the mistake. The size moves, not the stop.
wrong.Use full size anyway: Full size on a wide stop risks more than the rule allows.

questions.q: What was the weak spot?
questions.story: A break barely clears the line, closing 0.4% over it on thin volume. You buy it. Next day it closes back under the line.
choices: A thin break barely clearing the line
questions.answer: A thin break barely clearing the line
questions.why: A thin break that barely cleared the line. A break with volume matters more than one without, and this kind closes back under.
questions.lesson_line: A barely-there break on thin volume is a weak break.

wrong.The stop was too tight: The stop followed the rule. The weakness was the break itself.
wrong.Nothing; breaks just fail: Some do, but this one showed its weakness before the buy: thin volume and a close barely over the line.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought a break 10 trading days ago. It sits at 0.6R after three flat closes with no higher high.
choices: Hold; the stop has not traded
questions.answer: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold. No follow-through within a few sessions is itself the signal.
questions.lesson_line: No follow-through is the signal. Free the money.

wrong.Hold; the stop has not traded: The time stop is its own exit. Under 1R after 10 days, the money goes elsewhere.
wrong.Add; it is cheap: A break is never an add. And no follow-through is a weak sign.

questions.q: Take the break?
questions.story: Lows rise into the falling line for three weeks, and volume fades each day. Today it pokes through.
choices: No; it is wedging up into the line
questions.answer: No; it is wedging up into the line
questions.why: No. Rising lows into the line on shrinking volume is not the tight drift down this setup wants.
questions.lesson_line: Wedging up into the line is not a tight drift down.

wrong.Yes; it broke the line: Breaking the line is not enough. The shape into it has to be a tight drift down.
wrong.Yes, if volume picks up: The wedge up into the line is the problem, and volume on the day does not fix the shape.

questions.q: A break gives no price target. What takes its place?
choices: Trims at 3R and 5R, then a trail
questions.answer: Trims at 3R and 5R, then a trail
questions.why: Trims at 3R and 5R, then a trail. Brandt: a trendline violation does not carry with it a price target.
questions.lesson_line: No target from the pattern. The R-based trims do the job.

wrong.The height of the pullback: A measuring rule is not ours. The trims are set in R.
wrong.The old high, all out: The old high is overhead supply, not a target. We trim in thirds and trail the rest.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 1%. Buy 109.23, stop 106.79. How many shares?
questions.why: 204. Account times risk percent, divided by the buy minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You hold the last third of a fast mover after both trims. Today it closes under its 10-day.
choices: Sell the last third on that close
questions.answer: Sell the last third on that close
questions.why: Sell the last third. A fast mover trails the 10-day, and we sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: The trail is a close under the 10-day. Sell it.

wrong.Hold until the 50-day breaks: The trail is the 10-day for a fast mover, not the 50-day.
wrong.Move the stop down: The stop only moves up, never down or wider.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 39.00. It gaps open at 38.20, and the first 30-minute low is 37.80.
questions.answer: Out; the loss is past 2R
questions.why: Out. On a gap through the stop the first 30-minute low is the new stop, but past 2R you get out. A low of 37.80 is more than 2R from 40.00.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop has a ceiling of 2R.

wrong.The new stop is 37.80: The 30-minute low is the stop only while the loss is inside 2R. This one is past it.
wrong.Hold; gaps fill: Hope is not a rule. The gap rule has a ceiling, and this is past it.

questions.q: On one stock we take at most 3 tries a week and 6 a month.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. After a stop-out, only a new trigger buys it again, and the cap is 3 tries a week and 6 a month on one stock.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week, six a month. Then leave it alone.

questions.q: Buy it?
questions.story: A clean break sets up for tomorrow. The company reports after the close in 2 days.
choices: No; no buys 3 days before a report
Yes, and sell before the report
questions.answer: No; no buys 3 days before a report
questions.why: No. No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. Hold through one only if the trade is up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Stay three days clear of the report, or wait.

wrong.Yes; the line is clean: A clean line does not move the earnings window.
wrong.Yes, and sell before the report: The rule is no new buy in that window, not a quick trade through it.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You are up 4R in four days on a vertical, wide-range burst.
choices: Sell a big part into the burst
Hold it all; the trail will handle it
questions.answer: Sell a big part into the burst
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. A climax run on your own long is a judgment call, and selling a big part is the rule.
questions.lesson_line: A vertical burst is for selling into.

wrong.Add; it is going parabolic: A break is never an add, and a burst is for selling into.
wrong.Hold it all; the trail will handle it: The trail catches the turn late. A burst is the moment to bank a big part.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought at 30.00 with the stop at 29.00. It trades to 33.00.
choices: Sell a third and move the stop to 30.00
Sell half and trail the rest
questions.answer: Sell a third and move the stop to 30.00
questions.why: Sell a third at 3R and move the stop to breakeven, 30.00. The next third waits for 5R.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, then the stop to breakeven.

wrong.Sell half and trail the rest: The rule is a third at 3R and a third at 5R, not half at once.
wrong.Hold all until 5R: Holding it all risks a 3R gain for a scratch. The first third comes off at 3R.

questions.q: You followed every rule. What was the loss?
questions.story: You bought through an 83-session line at 18.79 with the stop at 18.53. The break closed only 0.39% over the line. Next day the low was 18.39.
choices: A planned loss; the stop did its job
A mistake; the stop was too tight
A reason to redraw the line
questions.answer: A planned loss; the stop did its job
questions.why: A planned loss. The stop is the exit and it did its job. A break that barely clears the line is a weak one.
questions.lesson_line: A stop that trades is the plan working.

wrong.A mistake; the stop was too tight: The stop sits a few cents under the day's low by the rule. Widening it to dodge a loss is the mistake.
wrong.A reason to redraw the line: Redrawing the line to get back in is the named mistake. Only a new trigger buys again.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
questions.story: You bought at 145.75 with the stop at 144.17, so 3R is 150.49. The next session opens at 152.00.
choices: Sell a third at the open
questions.answer: Sell a third at the open
questions.why: Sell a third at the open. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open. The stock then fell to 144.06 and the stop traded, but the trim had banked a gain.
questions.lesson_line: Take the trim the open hands you.

wrong.Hold; wait for the close: The level is already passed. Waiting gave the gap time to fill.
wrong.Sell it all: A third at 3R. The rest waits for 5R and the trail.

questions.q: Where is the buy?
questions.story: A stock doubles in a few weeks, then forms a tight, shallow flag. A falling line crosses the flag's highs.
questions.answer: Over the pattern's highest high
questions.why: Over the pattern's highest high. The flag's trendline break fails too often on a high tight flag, so buy the pattern's highest high instead.
questions.lesson_line: On a high tight flag, buy the pattern high, not the line.

wrong.Through the falling line: On a high tight flag the flag's trendline break fails too often. That is the named mistake.
wrong.At the 50-day average: A doubled stock holds far above its 50-day. The buy is on strength, over the high.

questions.q: You were stopped out. What now?
questions.story: You bought at 200.06 with the stop at 197.41. The low was 197.22, 19 cents under the stop. It closed 209.53 and reached 217 within a week.
choices: Only a new trigger buys it again
questions.answer: Only a new trigger buys it again
questions.why: Only a new trigger. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule.
questions.lesson_line: It ran without you. Only a new trigger buys it back.

wrong.Buy it back; it ran 6%: Chasing what ran is the mistake. A re-entry needs a new trigger.
wrong.Move your next stop lower: The stop is a few cents under the day's low. Moving it lower to avoid a stop-out is not the rule.

questions.q: What does the quiet volume say?
questions.story: A clean line of 3 touches over 85 sessions breaks, but on only 0.86x the 50-day average volume.
choices: Weak; a break with volume matters more
questions.answer: Weak; a break with volume matters more
questions.why: Weak. A trendline break with volume matters more than a break without. This quiet one is a poor sign.
questions.lesson_line: Volume confirms the break. A quiet break is a weak one.

wrong.Nothing; volume is noise: The Insider says a break with volume matters more than one without.
wrong.Strong; no one is selling: Quiet volume on a break is not strength. Buyers did not show up.

questions.q: Take the break?
questions.story: A steep three-week drop leaves two lower highs. A line through them breaks today.
choices: Pass; steep, short, two close highs
questions.answer: Pass; steep, short, two close highs
questions.why: Pass. Buying breaks of steep lines is a named mistake, and two highs this close may be nothing more than noise.
questions.lesson_line: A steep plunge draws a steep line. Skip it.

wrong.Take it; the line broke: The steeper the line, the less valid it is. A break of it is not enough.
wrong.Take it, on half size: Size does not repair a steep line with two close highs.

questions.q: The stop traded. Did the rules fail?
questions.story: A leader breaks a line you bought at 48.12 with the stop at 47.25. The next session is the first day of a market break, and the stop trades.
choices: No; a planned loss, rules followed
Yes; the stop was too wide
questions.answer: No; a planned loss, rules followed
questions.why: No. The break was valid by every gate and the stop did its job. The next session was the first day of the February 2020 market break.
questions.lesson_line: A valid break can lose. The stop makes it small.

wrong.Yes; we should have waited: A later buy is a different trade with a wider stop. The loss here was the planned 1.80%.
wrong.Yes; the stop was too wide: The stop was 1.80% away, inside the 3% a stop usually sits within.

questions.q: With a fixed stop and no trims, 78.8% of this scan's triggers were eventually stopped. What does that show?
choices: Trims and a trail bank the gains
The line is a bad signal
questions.answer: Trims and a trail bank the gains
questions.why: Trims and a trail bank the gains. A fixed stop without trims gives winners back, though 54.2% reached 3R first.
questions.lesson_line: Bank a third at 3R and 5R. Trail the rest.

wrong.The line is a bad signal: Over half reached 3R. The exits, not the entry, gave it back.
wrong.Wider stops would win more: A wider stop means fewer shares, not more winners.

questions.q: Write the plan.
questions.story: MSFT, January 2012: a mega-cap drifts tight under a five-month falling line, then trades through it.
choices: Wait for a close 3% past the line
questions.answer: Buy 26.97, stop 26.73, a third at 3R
questions.why: Buy at market, 26.97. Stop a few cents under the day's low, 26.73. A third comes off at 3R. MSFT got there the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open.

wrong.Buy 26.97, stop 25.00, hold it all: The stop belongs a few cents under the day's low, 26.73. And a third comes off at 3R.
wrong.Wait for a close 3% past the line: We do not wait for a close 3% past the line. The trigger is the trade through it.

questions.q: Which gets the bigger size?
questions.story: Two valid breaks. A: a leader tight under the line, room overhead, Green market. B: Yellow market, the stop 4% away, a key level just above.
choices: B; it has the wider stop
Equal; the line is the same
questions.answer: A; every cue lines up
questions.why: A. Tight under the line on drying volume, room to the first anchor high and a Green market is the A+ end. A Yellow market, a stop 3% to 5% away and a key level just above grade B.
questions.lesson_line: Same line, different grade. The spot and the market set the size.

wrong.B; it has the wider stop: A wider stop grades it down, and so does the key level just above.
wrong.Equal; the line is the same: The line is the same, but the market, the stop and the room are not.

questions.q: Is this the first break?
questions.story: Two weeks ago a stock closed over its falling line, then slid back under. Today it trades through the line again.
choices: Yes; it is a fresh day
questions.answer: No; it already closed through
questions.why: No. A first break has no daily close above the line before the trigger day. A close two weeks ago means this is not the first.
questions.lesson_line: One close over the line spends the first break.

wrong.Yes; a wick is allowed: A wick is allowed, but a close above the line is not. This one closed over it.
wrong.Yes; it is a fresh day: The rule counts closes above the line since the first anchor, not days.

questions.q: Price reached the start of the line 77% of the time, so we sell all at that old high.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The old high is overhead supply, context and not a rule. No pattern target replaces the R-based trims.
questions.lesson_line: The old high is supply to respect, not a target.

questions.q: Take the break?
questions.story: A clean break of a long line in a stock with an RS rating of 55, in a lagging group.
choices: No; the stock is not a leader
questions.answer: No; the stock is not a leader
questions.why: No. We buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups. A clean line in a laggard is still a laggard.
questions.lesson_line: The stock comes before the line.

wrong.Yes; the line is clean: A clean line is only one of the gates. The RS rating is another.
wrong.Yes, with a smaller stop: A smaller stop does not make a laggard a leader.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. A pullback drifts tight under a falling line. Above its 200-day? Take the break or pass.
choices: Take it; above the 200-day, tight drift
Pass; the stock is under the 200-day
Pass; the line is a flat top
questions.answer: Take it; above the 200-day, tight drift
questions.why: Take it. The close sits above the 200-day and the pullback drifts tight under a shallow line. The break ran straight to new highs.
questions.lesson_line: The 200-day and the tight drift first. Then the line.

wrong.Pass; the stock is under the 200-day: Look again: price sits above the 200-day here.
wrong.Pass; the line is a flat top: The line falls, slowly. A slow slope is still a slope.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. A good-looking falling line. Is the stock above its 200-day? Take the break or pass.
choices: Take it; the line is long
Take it; the volume is fine
questions.answer: Pass; it is under the 200-day
questions.why: Pass. The close was 4.9% under the 200-day, so the line does not matter. A good-looking line under a flat 200-day is not our break.
questions.lesson_line: A fine line under the 200-day is still a pass.

wrong.Take it; the line is long: A long line is only one gate. The 200-day is another.
wrong.Take it; the volume is fine: Fine volume does not lift a stock over its 200-day.

questions.q: Which one do we take?
questions.story: Four breaks today. A: under its 200-day. B: reports in 2 days. C: a leader, tight under the line. D: gaps 5% over the line.
choices: A; the line is the longest
C; a leader tight under the line
questions.answer: C; a leader tight under the line
questions.why: C. A stock under the 200-day, a report inside 3 days and a gap over 4% each rule one out. C is the leader that is tight under the line.
questions.lesson_line: Run every gate. One failure ends it.

wrong.A; the line is the longest: It is under the 200-day. A long line does not fix that.
wrong.B; the volume is biggest: A report inside 3 days ends it. Big volume does not move the window.
wrong.D; it has momentum: A gap more than 4% over the line is no trade.
